one_month_reasoning: Two scheduled events very likely fall inside the window to 2026-10-30. (1) The Q1 FY27 print. The date is unconfirmed, but past years (Wed Oct 29 2025, Wed Oct 30 2024) point to Oct 28 or 29 after the close. The guide restated in the Sep 2 8-K is revenue of $89.85-90.95B, Azure +44-45% cc on the new definition and capex over $50B. This year's pattern is a beat followed by a reaction set by capex and FCF: the stock fell after the Q2 and Q3 FY26 prints despite beats. So I treat the earnings move as roughly symmetric with fat tails. (2) The Oct 27-28 FOMC. I had ~56% hike odds from a pre-PCE blog snapshot. After the softer Sep 30 PCE, swaps price ~36% (Bloomberg) and CME FedWatch about 47%. Prediction markets were 68-69% as of Sep 29, before the print. The rate headwind is therefore smaller and more two-sided than I had, and the +1.8% on Sep 30 already reflects it. Smaller items: the Sept jobs report (Oct 2) and CPI (mid-October). Post-earnings drift from the July beat and positive momentum (+48% off the June low) add a small positive tilt. Net: median about $521 (+0.5%) and roughly 9.5-10% effective one-month vol (a core of 8.5% plus a 25% fat-tail component at 1.6x, because earnings are in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (Sep-2027 NTM EPS $23.7 x 23.5 = $558, weight 0.5), a SOTP (core $23.7 x 22x = $522, plus the 25% OpenAI stake at about $1.1T less a 25% haircut = $28, less $4.4 of net debt including finance leases = $545, weight 0.3) and a TTM-multiple reversion ($20.56 x 26.5 = $545, weight 0.2). Blended: $551.

Today's forward P/E is about 25x. The 2022 hiking-cycle trough was about 20x forward (26.5x TTM), and the 10-year TTM range is 21-62, with median 32.5. The Fed is still in a hiking cycle (CME: ~52% odds of another 25bp by year-end, even after the softer PCE). A year from now, with FY28 growth decelerating and capex still rising, I expect about 1.5 turns of compression, not reversion to the mean.

methods.inputs: Historical-multiple reversion: TTM EPS at 2027-09-30 = 0.75 x FY27 $19.76 + 0.25 x FY28 $22.97 = $20.56, x 26.5x TTM

The 10-year average is 31.4 and the median 32.5. The June-2022 hiking-cycle low was 26.5x, and the stock is at 28.3 today. With a rate regime similar to 2022 (Fed hiking with CPI at 3.4%), I anchor on that cycle's low rather than the long-run average. Down from 27x in round 1 because heavier FY27 capex (above the CY26 $175B) keeps FCF conversion low.

bear.story: The AI capex ROI scare returns as FY27 capex grows above the CY26 ~$175B and operating-lease commitments ($329B uncommenced) weigh. OpenAI (about 38-41% of RPO, now free to use any cloud) shifts incremental workloads away or its round stalls. The Fed keeps hiking. The multiple compresses to about 18x a cut NTM EPS of about $21.5. This repeats the June-2026 low ($349) and the 2022 drawdown (-37%).

base.story: Azure grows 40%+ as capacity lands, and FY27 EPS of about $19.8 is delivered with the operating margin down less than 1pt. FY28 comes in slightly under consensus on depreciation. The multiple settles near 23.5x forward on NTM EPS of about $23.7. The OpenAI stake is marked via a private round at about $1.1-1.4T with no IPO yet.

bull.story: The $678B RPO converts with ex-OpenAI RPO growing 25%+, Copilot and agents monetize, and FCF inflects as capex growth slows in FY28. OpenAI prices a round at $1.4T or more, so the stake is worth $45+/share gross. Rates stabilize and the multiple re-rates toward about 28-29x forward on $24+ EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $395 (about 17x the haircut FY28 EPS and about 20x FY27 consensus, near the 2022 hiking-cycle trough multiple), the market would be pricing an earnings downgrade rather than multiple noise. Likely causes: Azure decelerating below about 30%, OpenAI cutting or repricing its roughly $270-280B RPO commitment under its any-cloud rights, or FY27 capex rising while revenue guidance falls. The June-2026 low of $349 came with earnings intact, so judge a break by estimate cuts, not price alone.

reasoning: Base-rate anchor: MSFT's 1-year realized vol is 32%, and large caps typically move 25-35% a year. MSFT drawdowns average about 17% with a median recovery of about 4 months (Trefis). The deep ones (2000, 2008, 2022 at -37%) came in rate or valuation shocks. The stock has just gone through a -37% AI-capex drawdown and recovered 48%, similar to 2022-23. The supervisor's corrections change my inputs in both directions. (a) The ~$175B capex is calendar-2026 and FY27 capex grows, so I haircut FY28 EPS by 3% and cut the TTM reversion multiple to 26.5x. (b) The OpenAI stake is 25%, not 27%, but OpenAI is now reported to be raising at about $1.4T, so I value the stake at 25% of ~$1.1T less 25%, which is $28/share. That is almost unchanged, and it is set by the funding rounds, not the thin Polymarket market. (c) Net debt including finance leases is about $33B, which subtracts about $4/share; my Fool-sourced $129B figure mixed debt with leases. (d) OpenAI's RPO share is about 38-41%, not 45%, with ex-OpenAI RPO +25%: slightly less concentration risk, but OpenAI's any-cloud right keeps it real. (e) October hike odds fell to ~36% after PCE, so the macro overlay is less hostile, although the Fed is still in a hiking cycle. I also fixed an error in my own work: at 2027-09-30 the NTM EPS is 0.75 x FY28 + 0.25 x FY29 ($23.7), not the FY27/FY28 mix I used. That raises the EPS base about 5%, and I offset it with a lower forward multiple (23.5x vs 25x), justified by the 2022 hiking-cycle trough of ~20x forward and slower FY29 growth. Blended fair value is $551 (+6%). I set the distribution median at about $544 (+5%), a small haircut to fair value for concentration and capex risk. It is a lognormal core at 27% vol plus a 20% fat-tail component at 1.6x (about 31% effective, in line with realized). That gives P(>=518) = 0.567 and P(>=700) = 0.196. Scenario mean is about $552 (bear $385 at 25%, base $555 at 50%, bull $715 at 25%), consistent with the ladder. Research in round 2 was limited to three searches; Bloomberg is paywalled and was read via search summaries.
